answer: Require every agent to stake a refundable deposit before its first voyage into the marketplace, with the stake locked for a fixed cooling period. One identity can hold only one active stake, so creating many fake agents means locking real funds for each. Each verified transaction leaves a small ripple of reputation tied to that stake, like a quill signing every entry in a public ledger. If an agent is caught cheating, its stake is slashed and its reputation wiped, so a Sybil attacker must pay fresh capital for every new identity while honest agents keep their deposit intact.
